items.title: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?
items.summary: Spanish women’s refusal to surrender hard-won rights helped Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez clinch an unlikely victory in a snap election three years ago. As he gambles with another early vote on Sunday, his hopes of defying the odds rest on women again rallying to block the far right from governing Spain for the first time since Francisco Franco’s dictatorship.
items.t: With Spain’s far right on the cusp of power, can women bail Sanchez out once again?

items.title: Trump says he's giving Iran "a chance to be smart"
items.summary: Trump says victory over Iran will come "whenever I want it," but he's giving the regime "a chance to be smart" while his threat of new strikes looms.
items.t: Trump says he's giving Iran "a chance to be smart"

items.title: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections
items.summary: Political violence is escalating in Nigeria ahead of the general elections scheduled for January. Candidates and their supporters have increasingly come under attack, with armed groups disrupting campaign rallies and some assaults resulting in deaths. Despite the growing number of incidents, security forces have struggled to contain the violence. With less than two months to go before the vote, fears are mounting that intimidation and deadly attacks could prevent many Nigerians from freely taking part in the democratic process.
items.t: Nigeria: Political violence and attacks on candidates raise fears ahead of January elections

items.title: Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez confident of election victory despite polls – Europe live
items.summary:
‘I can’t conceive of us losing,’ the leader said

Freelance journalist based in Madrid and host of the Sobremesa podcast

Vox has often been portrayed in international coverage as a party of Franco nostalgists whose ultraconservative Catholicism and civil-war rhetoric towards the separatist Catalan “enemy within” threatened a return to the worst of Spain’s recent past.

items.t: Trump calling Putin ‘friend’ like declaring friendship with Hitler during WW2, Zelenskyy says – Europe live

items.title: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols
items.summary:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights

Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights.

In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning, the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights.

Continue reading...
items.t: Canada’s top court upholds Quebec law barring public sector workers from wearing religious symbols

items.title: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico
items.summary: President Claudia Sheinbaum blasted the DEA after it set up anonymous tip lines in the country, accusing American officials of interference.
items.t: U.S. opens hotline for tips about cartels, angering Mexico

items.title: Student movement in France: "The situation has varied greatly from one school to another"
items.summary: Thousands of high school and university students gathered at Place de la Bastille in Paris on Thursday. A protest movement that disrupted schools earlier this term prompted the government to announce 20,000 additional university places and reforms to the admissions process. But demonstrators say these measures do not go far enough, calling for a university place for every applicant. We discuss the situation on the ground with Jean-Rémi Girard, a high school teacher and Vice-President of SNALC-FGAF.
items.t: Student movement in France: "The situation has varied greatly from one school to another"

items.title: Bulgarian fans injured after clashes between supporters at Marseille-Levski game in Europa League
items.summary: French and Bulgarian authorities condemned the violence that left at least 11 Bulgarian soccer fans injured during clashes between Marseille and Levski Sofia supporters before their Europa League match on Thursday evening, and Marseille prosecutors opened two investigations.
items.t: Bulgarian fans injured after clashes between supporters at Marseille-Levski game in Europa League

items.title: Black Friday: How the global shopping phenomenon is evolving amid the cost-of-living crisis
items.summary: Online spending on Black Friday is expected to rise by 9.2% year-on-year to $12.9 billion, driven by increased use of Buy Now, Pay Later options and steep discounts on televisions, toys and furniture, according to Adobe's initial forecast. But with promotions now running throughout the year, are consumers experiencing deal fatigue? And how is the cost-of-living crisis shaping their shopping habits? We discuss these questions with Hilary Ingham, Head of Department and Professor of Economics at Lancaster University.
items.t: Black Friday: How the global shopping phenomenon is evolving amid the cost-of-living crisis

items.title: Under a new flag, North Korea carves out identity as fully fledged nuclear state
items.summary: North Korea has modified its national flag as part of a constitutional amendment. The text also enshrined the country's status as a nuclear power and removed any reference to the "peaceful reunification" pursued by Kim Jong Un's predecessors. Meanwhile, the reclusive leader has been keen to demonstrate his desire to expand diplomatic ties with friendly nations. Yuka Royer speaks with Edward Howell of Oxford University to put these recent developments into context.
items.t: Under a new flag, North Korea carves out identity as fully fledged nuclear state

items.title: France: David Lisnard shakes up presidential race
items.summary: David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes and a candidate in France's 2027 presidential election, has climbed to third place in several opinion polls. His rise is shaking up the political landscape on the right and centre. We discuss what this means with France 24's James André.
items.t: France: David Lisnard shakes up presidential race

items.title: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong
items.summary: The tiny Vallarta mud turtle was only discovered in 2018. It's critically endangered with around 300 thought to live in the wild. Almost one tenth of that number were stashed in a traveler's luggage, bound in duct tape.
items.t: Dutch authorities seize 26 critically endangered turtles from luggage of passenger bound for Hong Kong

items.title: Ukraine: How much have Europeans spent on aid?
items.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, EU member states have provided around €200 billion in aid to Ukraine, making them its largest contributors ahead of the United States. Germany leads in total financial contributions, with around €54 billion, roughly twice France's €27 billion. But the picture changes when aid is measured against GDP or per capita, with Denmark and other Nordic countries ranking among the biggest contributors.
items.t: Ukraine: How much have Europeans spent on aid?

items.title: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights
items.summary:
Norwegian airline tells customers not to come to airports after surging fuel costs caused by Iran war ruin finances

Norse Atlantic Airways has filed for bankruptcy and cancelled all future flights after surging fuel costs caused by the Iran war ruined its finances.

The Norwegian airline said it was entering insolvency and posted a message on its website telling customers not to come to airports – including passengers stranded away from home. Its collapse came a day after it put flights on hold with a warning that its finances were critical.

Continue reading...
items.t: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all future flights

items.title: Too old for soft toys? Tell that to kidults booking up the Harrods Jellycat cafe
items.summary:
Department stores are hosting in-person events for those who find comfort in collecting the British soft toy brand

They’re cute, cuddly and taking over the homes of young adults.

Jellycat, a British soft toy brand founded in 1999, is experiencing a rise in interest from adult buyers as they snap up signature smiley designs in the shape of everything from croissants and disco balls to turtles and teabags.

items.t: Too old for soft toys? Tell that to kidults booking up the Harrods Jellycat cafe

items.title: With new law, Iraq sees rise in child marriage, custody battles
items.summary: In January 2025, Iraq's parliament passed an amendment allowing families to place their household under religious law, governing all issues around marriage, divorce and inheritance. The new Ja'fari law, a Shiite law, came into force in October 2025. One year on, its consequences have been raising serious alarm, especially among women, who say they've seen a major rollback of their rights. FRANCE 24's Marie-Charlotte Roupie reports, with Josh Vardey.
items.t: With new law, Iraq sees rise in child marriage, custody battles

items.title: ‘Mass-casualty event’ in Europe possible amid rise in Russian sabotage, says thinktank
items.summary:
Report warns attacks on critical infrastructure could lead to demand for retaliation and expose EU divisions

Russian sabotage attacks on Europe are increasing and a “mass-casualty event” is now possible as increasingly skilled operatives target critical infrastructure with ever more complex methods, a leading strategic thinktank has said.

The International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) said in a report that Russian intelligence services and their proxies were targeting European railways, energy networks and defence industries in an attempt to weaken support for Ukraine.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Mass-casualty event’ in Europe possible amid rise in Russian sabotage, says thinktank

items.title: Japan's radical past: Retracing the far-left groups of the 1970s
items.summary: Our correspondents delve into the history of Japan's radical left in the 1970s. From the United Red Army to the Japanese Red Army, several movements turned to armed struggle and violent action. More than half a century on, our team met with two former militants.
items.t: Japan's radical past: Retracing the far-left groups of the 1970s

items.title: Investigator says Russia is "brainwashing" Ukrainian children at so-called summer camps
items.summary: Since Russia's invasion of Ukraine, many Ukrainian children have ended up at Russian camps where the Ukrainian language is banned and the Russian anthem is played each day. More Sunday on 60 Minutes.
items.t: Investigator says Russia is "brainwashing" Ukrainian children at so-called summer camps

items.t: Trump slams foes and threatens future vetoes in Thanksgiving posts

items.title: Iranian women are facing not just lashings, but "honor killings"
items.summary: Singer Parastoo Ahmadi's 74 lashes for daring to sing without her hair covered is not a unique case in Iran. Other women are being killed, some by their own families.
items.t: Iranian women are facing not just lashings, but "honor killings"

items.title: Airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy, succumbing to aviation fuel costs
items.summary: The low-cost airline was only founded a few years ago and had been struggling to turn a profit. The spike in aviation fuel prices caused by the war in Iran has now driven Norway's Norse Atlantic into bankruptcy.

items.summary: War, poverty and disrupted schooling could put more girls in Iran at risk of child marriage, rights advocates have warned.

items.title: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos
items.summary: Severe storms battered the US East Coast on Thursday, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and coastal flooding. Nearly one million homes were left without power, while hundreds of flights were cancelled and thousands delayed during one of the country's busiest travel periods. The weather also forced the postponement of New York's Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade until Saturday.
items.t: US: Thanksgiving storms cause flooding and travel chaos

items.title: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon
items.summary: Once defined by crowds queuing outside shops for one-off bargains, Black Friday has evolved into weeks of online promotions. As discounts spread throughout the year, consumers are becoming more cautious about advertised deals, increasingly turning to AI and price comparisons to find genuine bargains. Camille Knight looks at the origins of the global shopping phenomenon.
items.t: Black Friday: The evolution of a shopping phenomenon

items.title: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter
items.summary: As Russia continues to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure, residents are preparing for another difficult winter of strikes and power cuts. With supply chains under pressure, food prices are also rising, forcing many Ukrainians to cut back on essentials or stock up ahead of the coming months.
items.t: Ukraine: Residents brace for another difficult winter

items.title: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate
items.summary: Spain goes to the polls on Sunday in an early parliamentary election that may usher in a right-wing coalition to replace the Socialist-led minority government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, one of Europe's last leftist leaders. Our correspondent Sarah Morris tells us more.
items.t: Spain election: Housing crisis and immigration dominate final campaign debate

items.summary:

items.summary: Gadi ​Eisenkot's Yashar party and a left-wing faction agreed on a preliminary coalition deal on Thursday, after a brief dispute that had posed a challenge to his bid to unseat Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu following an inconclusive election last month. items.title: ‘Crisis in empathy’: prison guard was watching TV while Aboriginal man was dying in custody, NSW coroner finds
items.summary:
Judge says officers should be banned from screens and phones while on shift after the 33-year-old’s death at Silverwater

• Warning: This article contains references to Indigenous Australians who have died

The NSW coroner has found the death of an Aboriginal man in custody in 2023 was not only preventable but was “one of the most egregious deaths” she had investigated.

Corrective Services NSW has been recommended to overhaul officer training for self-harm responses, and ban officers’ access to TV and YouTube while on shift.

items.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks
items.summary: The number of Indians working in Germany has grown rapidly in recent years. But many continue to face challenges in the labor market. Some also fall victim to recruitment scams, leaving them vulnerable to exploitation.

items.title: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners
items.summary: South Africa was once a welcoming country; a refuge for those fleeing conflict and persecution. But for thousands of foreigners, the dream of a new life in South Africa is turning into more of a nightmare. Against a backdrop of unemployment and economic hardship, anti-immigration movements are gaining ground. Our correspondents report.
items.t: Immigration: South Africa no longer an El Dorado for foreigners

items.title: Spain’s Pedro makes final campaign push to beat the right ahead of crunch vote
items.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez makes his final campaign push with a rally in Madrid Friday, the last day of campaigning for Sunday's high-stakes elections. Opinion polls show the Socialist premier lagging behind the main right-wing Popular Party (PP) as the Spanish vote opens an electoral cycle over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the EU.
items.t: Spain’s Pedro makes final campaign push to beat the right ahead of crunch vote

items.title: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations
items.summary:
Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday

King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean.

The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach.

Continue reading...
items.t: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations

items.title: Israel's Eisenkot and left-wing party agree coalition deal

items.title: Spain general election 2026: Could Sánchez lose power?
items.summary: Spanish voters head to the polls in just three days for a snap election, after eight years of Socialist-led rule. items.title: Mad about mara: the DIY dance movement helping young Nigerians escape the daily grind
items.summary:
What started as one artist’s response to being cut out of a music video has exploded, becoming a driving force in Nigeria’s cultural landscape

As a student in the central Nigerian city of Ilorin, Lawal Habeeb Kola loved staying in his hostel room to produce beats rather than returning to his family house in Lagos, the more frenetic city of his birth.

In 2022, one of his beats became popular on TikTok, and a version featuring ad-libbed vocals from a hypeman sent it viral. He was invited to the music video shoot in Lagos and thought his big break had finally come, but when the video was released, he was absent.

items.title: New Zealand election: final results show ruling coalition needs minor party to govern

Incumbent prime minister Christopher Luxon loses majority and needs support of Opportunity party to remain in power, or country faces another election

The final results of New Zealand’s general election show the incumbent rightwing coalition will need the support of a centrist newcomer party to form a government, and to avoid sending the country back to the polls.

Preliminary results on 7 November handed the National party and its two coalition partners, the populist New Zealand First and libertarian Act parties, a slim two-seat majority, making the election too close to call until final votes were tallied.

items.title: Threat from China looms large over Taiwan’s local elections

Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party

Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage.

Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years, are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.

The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid?

Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.

items.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
items.summary:
Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’, while Brazil ‘will not yield to this type of threat’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.

Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.

items.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
items.summary:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

items.summary:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.summary:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
items.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

items.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

items.summary:
Abelardo de la Espriella to take control of operation trying to free at least 20 hostages

Colombia’s president has arrived at the scene of an hours-long standoff between security services and gunmen holding at least 20 people hostage inside a supermarket in Cartagena, a popular tourist city.

Abelardo de la Espriella’s motorcade arrived in Cartagena on Tuesday night, Agence France-Presse reported, where he will ostensibly take control of an operation involving scores of officers, the navy and special forces.

Salvadorian man, who was deported in March 2025 and returned to US after supreme court ruling, leaving of own volition for Spain

Kilmar Ábrego García has left the United States of his own volition, his lawyers confirmed on Tuesday, with the Department of Homeland Security confirming that he was travelling to Spain.

A source close to Ábrego said Madrid was his first stop but that it would not be his final destination.
